input: scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products; merge when done
task: Explore: open-tennis-robots flagship buildable item, sense an empty hopper (FLAG_HOPPER_EMPTY) and have the runner report it

doc_friction.issue: The buildable item named a break-beam sensor, but the feeder's ESP32 (WROOM-32) has no free GPIO besides UART0; nobody had checked the pin map against the item. The item was done instead from the existing tachometers.

deviations.why: The flagship row asked for a break-beam over the column (CAD and firmware). No pin is free for it (hardware/electronics.md), so the empty hopper is read from the launcher wheels' speed drop instead, with no CAD change.
deviations.did: controller.LaunchCheck judges each stroke by momentum-predicted wheel speed drop; no new hardware
deviations.result: 27-build simulated sweep: loaded strokes >= 1.26x threshold, dry <= 0.17x; drill runner stops on the first dry stroke

goal: Close the open-tennis-robots item where an empty tub ended a drill on a release timeout
notes: Explore idea: pinless empty-hopper detection. Every exposed GPIO on the feeder's ESP32 is taken, so a break-beam cannot be wired; a ball takes its momentum from the launcher wheels (8.8% per wheel flat, CAD figures), so the tachometers judge each stroke. Two failed variants recorded in firmware/esp32/README.md (4-rev mean + share 0.4: loaded down to 0.47x threshold at 1500 rpm on a heavy wheel; the Pi's final stop faked a launch until targets-change froze the watch). Verification: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -> 138 tests OK (56 s); node --test sim/page/usage 21 pass; fixtures unchanged; cad tests touching firmware config 3 passed (build123d 0.13.0 venv); tests/launch_check_sweep.py worst loaded 1.26, worst dry 0.167; check_post_frontmatter, check_post_links, post_similarity clean; portfolio/router/validate.py clean. Simulator-only; not measured on real wheels.
